title: Background & Mission
content:
I'm a third-year B.Tech CSE student in Roorkee. I build machine-learning systems and then try to break them: check the data before training, sign the model before loading it, watch for drift, and show where an answer came from.

Most of my projects are prototypes on synthetic data, and each page says so. I'm looking for an internship in security-focused data science, remote or on-site.

title: AegisZ: Problem
content:
Problem:
Clinical and welfare triage models need personal data to make decisions, but sending raw identifiers to external inference services breaks privacy commitments and exposes systems to extraction attacks. Privacy must be an architectural property of the system rather than an afterthought.

title: AegisZ: How it works
content:
How it works:
The gateway guarantees mathematical privacy and post-quantum integrity at every processing stage:

1. **Ingress:** Handles clinical records, social welfare applications, and HL7/EDI payloads through an authenticated interface.
2. **Threat detector:** ONNX Runtime engine (combining Isolation Forest and gradient boosting) screening for prompt injection, RBAC privilege escalation, anomalous velocity, and insider abuse before quarantine or dispatch.
3. **PII vault:** HMAC-SHA3-256 format-preserving pseudonymization coupled with Laplace differential privacy injecting calibrated noise (ε between 0.1 and 5.0).
4. **Isolated triage:** Domain inference models process strictly anonymized and sanitized feature tensors.
5. **Audit ledger:** Cryptographic SHA3-512 Merkle hash chain sealed with ML-DSA-65 post-quantum digital signatures (FIPS 204), ML-KEM-768 key encapsulation metadata (FIPS 203), and a public verification endpoint.
6. **CBOM scanner:** CycloneDX 1.6 Cryptographic Bill of Materials scanner auditing dependencies and flagging classical keys vulnerable to harvest-now-decrypt-later vectors.
7. **Command center:** React web UI streaming live audit logs over WebSockets; multi-architecture container images supporting x86_64 and linux/s390x.

title: Inferyx: Problem
content:
Problem:
Building the model is not the hard part. Understanding it, trusting it, monitoring it and knowing when it breaks is. Most tools stop once weights are saved; production systems fail after deployment when distribution shifts or unvalidated artifacts run unchecked.

title: Inferyx: How it works
content:
How it works:
The studio guides tabular data from initial ingestion through live inference packaging and production telemetry:

1. **Studio interface:** React 19 single-page studio across seven views (Overview, Data, Training, Results, Tracking, Monitoring, Tools) managed by four dedicated state contexts.
2. **API gateway:** FastAPI backend providing role-based access control with optional JWT tokens, API keys, and three permission tiers (viewer, editor, admin).
3. **Data engine:** Polars and PyArrow engine executing multi-format ingestion and parallel schema profiling in a single vectorized pass.
4. **Feature engineering:** Leak-free temporal rolling features, calendar extraction, lag generation, and strict TimeSeriesSplit evaluation.
5. **Execution worker:** Dual-mode worker dispatching via Celery and Redis when broker is reachable, falling back to an in-process thread pool with an automatic startup reaper for interrupted jobs.
6. **Training engine:** Optuna Bayesian hyperparameter search streaming real-time metrics over WebSockets to the UI with automatic HTTP polling fallback.
7. **Explainability:** SHAP summary values, permutation feature importances, threshold tuning curves, and comparative model leaderboard.
8. **Signed export:** Standalone bundle secured with HMAC-SHA256 signatures, packaging ONNX, Safetensors, and signed joblib files with a dedicated FastAPI inference service and Dockerfile.
9. **Monitoring:** Continuous PSI (Population Stability Index) and Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistical drift tests dispatching webhook notifications on distribution decay.

title: OrgMind: Overview & Goals
OrgMind: Problem
content:
Problem:
Enterprise search and agentic question-answering hallucinate citations or leak privileged documents across organizational silos. An answer without an auditable, permissions-filtered source node in an active knowledge graph is merely a guess.

title: OrgMind: How it works
content:
How it works:
The knowledge graph couples graph database queries with fine-grained access control and grounding checks:

1. **Ingestion pipeline:** Modular connector framework feeding an eight-stage retryable ingestion queue coordinated by arq workers and Redis.
2. **Dual persistence:** FalkorDB low-latency graph database operating over OpenCypher queries, synchronized with PostgreSQL 16 for identity, workspaces, execution jobs, and immutable audit logs.
3. **Grounded agent:** Provider-agnostic LiteLLM execution loop with strict grounding verification and allow-listed, parameterized Cypher tool execution.
4. **API and protocols:** FastAPI REST service and SSE event streams spanning 24 endpoints under OpenAPI 3.1, coupled with an MCP server exposing 11 query and analysis tools.
5. **Explorer UI:** Next.js 14 application featuring conversational question interface, Cytoscape graph visualization, decision lineage viewer, and peer reviews.
6. **Data governance:** Four authorization roles (admin, editor, viewer, auditor), untrusted-data delimiters neutralizing prompt injection vectors, two-phase role-gated mutations, and bitemporal record supersession instead of in-place deletion.

title: phenom: Overview & Goals
phenom: Problem
content:
Problem:
Cloud-based virtual assistants send everyday desktop context, notes, and commands to external servers. Exploring how much functionality can be driven purely locally tests privacy boundaries and offline machine-learning utility.

title: phenom: How it works
content:
How it works:
The project is structured around local inference with modular desktop interfaces:

1. **Inference backend:** Ollama local model service executing quantized language models on personal hardware.
2. **Interfaces:** Dual desktop access through a PyQt5 graphical interface and a local Flask web dashboard.
3. **Memory system:** Local SQLite database and flat file memory store preserving conversations and state.
4. **Tool modules:** System automation routines, hardware monitoring hooks, and experimental automation scripts.

title: RoadSaarthi: Problem
content:
Problem:
Infrastructure data only matters if someone acts on it. Raw telemetry from vehicle accelerometers and road cameras often ends up stranded in inspection logs rather than being prioritized, geolocated, and converted into dispatched municipal repair orders.

title: RoadSaarthi: How it works
content:
How it works:
The architecture translates continuous road roughness and pothole events into clustered municipal repairs:

1. **Event generator:** Synthetic telemetry generator emitting simulated accelerometer and GPS sensor hits every 300 seconds.
2. **Backend API:** FastAPI application utilizing SQLAlchemy 2 over PostgreSQL and PostGIS spatial indexing.
3. **Scoring engine:** Road Condition Index scoring module calculating localized segment degradation [[VERIFY: expand 'RPI']].
4. **Spatial clustering:** Scikit-learn DBSCAN algorithm grouping high-density surface defects into distinct spatial hotspots.
5. **Streaming bus:** WebSocket server broadcasting fresh incident clusters and severity recalculations.
6. **Command UI:** React and MapLibre GL mapping dashboard featuring seven operational views: command center, incident queue, road history, analytics, fleet inspection, work orders, and public reporting.

title: AI Threat Detection System: Problem
content:
Problem:
Most attacks look normal until you measure them across multiple statistical dimensions. Rule-based intrusion detection systems miss novel scanning behaviors and generate overwhelming alert volumes when high-throughput network flows fluctuate.

source: AI Threat Detection System (How it works)
title: AI Threat Detection System: How it works
content:
How it works:
The pipeline processes continuous network packets into classified flow anomalies:

1. **Traffic ingestion:** Synthetic network event generator emitting realistic background packets alongside malicious injection vectors.
2. **Flow analyzer:** Windowed streaming buffer extracting seven continuous flow features: port distributions, protocol ratios, packet byte sizes, flow duration, transmission rates, entropy metrics, and total byte volumes.
3. **Anomaly scoring:** Scikit-learn Isolation Forest algorithm calculating multidimensional isolation depths across sliding flow windows.
4. **Severity engine:** Calibrated thresholds mapping isolation scores into actionable low, medium, high, and critical threat levels.
5. **Alert dispatcher:** Notification bus triggering structured security event alerts and incident tracking.
6. **Dashboard:** Flask web application rendering interactive Plotly telemetry, live event feeds, and JSON REST endpoints.
